tarfile opened in streaming mode (mode='r|') did not stop at end of file when seeking, so parsing a crafted archive could take exponentially longer. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151981 with commit 7f0dc59 on the 3.11 branch, which makes _Stream.seek() in Lib/tarfile.py stop reading when a read returns no data: https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/7f0dc59c9a70f8f3b4da33d7c4a2ba552a7acc21 and first released it in CPython 3.11.16. The advisory is https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/AXPSKKTSRKXTTJULW3XSIC74WZNAAPPB/ and the CVE record is https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11972. The DHI python-3.11 packages for Alpine 3.23 carry a backport of that fix from 3.11.15-r10, made before the upstream 3.11.16 release. We checked every package built from source python-3.11 except python-3.11-doc and python-3.11-tests, in every published build for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 24 builds, 3.11.14-r0 to the current 3.11.18-r4, on x86_64 and aarch64, each against its index checksum. The python-3.11 package ships the module as /usr/lib/python3.11/tarfile.py. It has the end-of-file check that the fix adds to _Stream.seek() in 3.11.15-r10 and every later build, and lacks it in 3.11.14-r0 to 3.11.15-r9. The tarfile .pyc files in the python-3.11-pycache-pyc0, -pyc1 and -pyc2 packages are checked-hash .pyc files, and the source hash they record changes exactly where the tarfile.py source changes.

tarfile opened in streaming mode (mode='r|') did not stop at end of file when seeking, so parsing a crafted archive could take exponentially longer. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151981 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/3f031d431f80668e14f3bc066bbf4369cd9281b9), first released in CPython 3.13.15; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/AXPSKKTSRKXTTJULW3XSIC74WZNAAPPB/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11972. Compared Lib/tarfile.py in the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.13 package in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4) with the upstream CPython releases; both architectures agree. 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.14-r0 ship the unchanged upstream file, without the end-of-file check in _Stream.seek(). 3.13.14-r1 to 3.13.14-r3, CPython 3.13.14 builds, add that check as a backport made before the upstream 3.13.15 release. CVE-2026-11972: tarfile did not handle end of file properly for an archive opened in streaming mode (mode="r|"), so parsing a crafted archive could take exponentially longer. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151981 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e86666c9dd256d52d0fbef6feb1ea4a51768fdec), first released in CPython 3.14.7; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/AXPSKKTSRKXTTJULW3XSIC74WZNAAPPB/; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11972. Compared Lib/tarfile.py in every published build, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package on x86_64 and aarch64 with the files in the upstream CPython 3.14 releases. 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.6-r9 lack the fix; 3.14.6-r10 is the first published build that has it and carries a DHI backport of the upstream fix, ahead of the upstream release, and every later build carries it.

It has the end-of-file check that the fix adds to _Stream.seek() in 3.11.15-9 and every later build, and lacks it in 3.11.15-0 to 3.11.15-8. None of the checked packages ships a compiled tarfile module.

tarfile opened in streaming mode (mode='r|') did not stop at end of file when seeking, so parsing a crafted archive could take exponentially longer. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151981 with commit 7f0dc59 on the 3.11 branch, which makes _Stream.seek() in Lib/tarfile.py stop reading when a read returns no data: https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/7f0dc59c9a70f8f3b4da33d7c4a2ba552a7acc21 and first released it in CPython 3.11.16. The advisory is https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/AXPSKKTSRKXTTJULW3XSIC74WZNAAPPB/ and the CVE record is https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11972. The DHI python-3.11 packages for Debian 13 carry a backport of that fix from 3.11.15-9, made before the upstream 3.11.16 release.
